dedupe_keys.name: nemsis public release research dataset national ems information system

description: The NEMSIS Public-Release Research Dataset is the largest publicly available collection of emergency medical services (EMS) activation records in the United States. Each record is one EMS activation documented under the NEMSIS national data standard, with the national elements covering dispatch and response times, patient assessment, procedures, medications and disposition; the 2025 release holds 63,635,893 activations submitted by 14,801 EMS agencies serving 54 states and territories. The National EMS Information System is a program of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's Office of EMS, hosted by the University of Utah, which maintains the standard and the national repository to which states submit data voluntarily. Coverage: the United States, one calendar year per release, at event level; identifiers of patients, agencies, receiving hospitals and states are removed. Access: researchers request a dataset through a help desk ticket, one year for a first request, under terms of use; a user manual, data dictionary, SAS code and list of contributing states are published, and the EMS Data Cube gives aggregate views. Cost is not stated on the pages read. Caveats: states vary in which events they submit, submitted errors are reported but not corrected, and some elements are masked for privacy. Simulation uses: EMS demand, response-time and operations modelling for emergency response and capacity planning of ambulance services and hospitals. Related: ambulance simulation models such as JEMSS (catalogued as model-jemss) need call data of this kind.
